lines: Title: Construction of Direct Product of Fields

Let $\struct {F, +_F, \times_F}$ be a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] whose [[Definition:Field Zero|zero]] is $0$ and whose [[Definition:Multiplicative Identity|multiplicative identity]] is $1$.
Let $E = F \times F$ be the [[Definition:Cartesian Product|Cartesian product]] of $F$ with itself.
Let [[Definition:Field Addition|addition]] be defined on $E$ by:
:$\forall a, b, c, d \in F: \tuple {a, b} +_E \tuple {c, d} := \tuple {a +_F c, b +_F d}$
Let [[Definition:Field Product|multiplication]] be defined on $E$ by:
:$\forall a, b, c, d \in F: \tuple {a, b} \times_E \tuple {c, d} := \tuple {\paren {a \times_F c} +_F \paren {-\paren {b \times_F d} }, \paren {a \times_F d} +_F \paren {b \times_F c} }$

In order to define the structure rigorously, each of the [[Definition:Field Addition|field addition]] and [[Definition:Field Product|field multiplication]] [[Definition:Binary Operation|operations]] were explicitly stated in the above.
However, in order to simplify presentation, the [[Definition:Binary Operation|operations]] will be denoted in the following as:
{{eqn | q = \forall a, b, c, d \in F
| r = \tuple {a c - b d, a d + b c}
when it is clear from the context which operation is implied.
We check the criteria for $E$ to be a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].

First we note that $\struct {E, +_E}$ is the [[Definition:Group Direct Product|external group direct product]] $\struct {F, +_F} \times \struct {F, +_F}$, where $\struct {F, +_F}$ is an [[Definition:Abelian Group|Abelian group]].

Hence from [[External Direct Product of Abelian Groups is Abelian Group]] we have that $\struct {E, +_E}$ is an [[Definition:Abelian Group|Abelian group]] whose [[Definition:Identity Element|identity]] is $\tuple {0, 0}$.
Now we consider the [[Definition:Algebraic Structure with One Operation|algebraic structure]] $\tuple {E, \times_E}$.
We specifically wish to demonstrate that $\tuple {E^*, \times_E}$, where $E^* := E \setminus \tuple {0, 0}$, is an [[Definition:Abelian Group|Abelian group]].
Taking the [[Axiom:Group Axioms|group axioms]] in turn:
Let $\tuple {a, b}$ and $\tuple {c, d}$ be arbitrary [[Definition:Element|elements]] of $\tuple {E, \times_E}$.
:$\tuple {a, b} \times_E \tuple {c, d} := \tuple {\paren {a \times_F c} +_F \paren {-\paren {b \times_F d} }, \paren {a \times_F d} +_F \paren {b \times_F c} }$
Because $\struct {F, +_F}$ is a [[Definition:Group|group]], $+_F$ is a [[Definition:Closed Operation|closed operation]].
Because $\struct {F, \times_F}$ is a [[Definition:Group|group]], $\times_F$ is a [[Definition:Closed Operation|closed operation]].
:$\tuple {\paren {a \times_F c} +_F \paren {-\paren {b \times_F d} }, \paren {a \times_F d} +_F \paren {b \times_F c} } \in F \times F$
Thus $\tuple {a, b} \times_E \tuple {c, d} \in E$ and so $\tuple {E, \times_E}$ is [[Definition:Closed Algebraic Structure|closed]].
We specifically note that if $\tuple {a, b} = \tuple {0, 0}$ or $\tuple {c, d} = \tuple {0, 0}$, then:
| l = \tuple {a c - b d, a d + b c}
it follows that if either $c \ne 0$ or $d \ne 0$, then $a = b = 0$.
So for $\tuple {a, b} \tuple {c, d} = \tuple {0, 0}$ it must be the case that either $\tuple {a, b} = \tuple {0, 0}$ or $\tuple {c, d} = \tuple {0, 0}$.
Thus it follows that $\tuple {E, \times_E} \setminus \tuple {0, 0}$ is [[Definition:Closed Algebraic Structure|closed]].
{{eqn | q = \forall a, b, c, d, e, f \in F
{{eqn | r = \tuple {a c - b d, a d + b c} \tuple {e, f}
{{eqn | r = \tuple {\paren {a c - b d} e - \paren {a d + b c} f, \paren {a c - b d} f + \paren {a d + b c} e}
| r = \tuple {a c e - b d e - a d f - b c f, a c f - b d f + a d e + b c e}
| c = $F$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]]: $\times_F$ [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributes]] over $+_F$
{{eqn | q = \forall a, b, c, d, e, f \in F
{{eqn | r = \tuple {a, b} \tuple {c e - d f, c f + d e}
{{eqn | r = \tuple {a \paren {c e - d f} - b \paren {c f + d e}, a \paren {c f + d e} + b \paren {c e - d f} }
| r = \tuple {a c e - a d f - b c f - b d e, a c f + a d e + b c e - b d f}
| c = $F$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]]: $\times_F$ [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributes]] over $+_F$
Because $\struct {F, +_F}$ is an [[Definition:Abelian Group|Abelian group]], $+_F$ is a [[Definition:Commutative Operation|commutative operation]].
:$\paren {\tuple {a, b} \tuple {c, d} } \tuple {e, f} = \tuple {a, b} \paren {\tuple {c, d} \tuple {e, f} }$
In order for $\tuple {E^*, \times_E}$ to be a [[Definition:Group|group]], it must have an [[Definition:Identity Element|identity element]]
With that in mind, let $\tuple {x, y} \in E$ such that:
:$\forall \tuple {a, b} \in E: \tuple {x, y} \tuple {a, b} = \tuple {a, b} = \tuple {a, b} \tuple {x, y}$
| l = \tuple {x a - y b, x b + y a}
| l = x a b - y b b
| c = $F$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]]: $\times_F$ [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributes]] over $+_F$
| l = x a b + y a a
Because $F$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]], this means that:
Thus it has been shown that $\tuple {1, 0}$ is the [[Definition:Identity Element|identity element]] of $\tuple {E, \times_E}$.
Hence, directly, $\tuple {1, 0}$ is the [[Definition:Identity Element|identity element]] of $\tuple {E^*, \times_E}$.
We have that $\tuple {1, 0}$ is the [[Definition:Identity Element|identity element]] of $\tuple {E^*, \times_E}$.
We investigate the conditions under which, for any given $\tuple {a, b} \in E$, there exists $\tuple {x, y} \in E$ such that:
| l = \tuple {x a - y b, x b + y a}
| l = x a b - y b^2
| l = x a b + y a^2

Hence, for $\tuple {x, y}$ to be the [[Definition:Multiplicative Inverse in Field|multiplicative inverse]] of $\tuple {a, b}$, it is [[Definition:Necessary and Sufficient|necessary and sufficient]] that:
:$\forall \tuple {a, b} \in E \setminus \tuple {0, 0}: \tuple {a, b}^{-1} = \paren {\dfrac a {a^2 + b^2}, \dfrac {-b} {a^2 + b^2} }$

Thus every [[Definition:Element|element]] $\tuple {a, b}$ of $\tuple {E, \times_E} \setminus \tuple {0, 0}$ has an [[Definition:Inverse Element|inverse]] $\paren {\dfrac a {a^2 + b^2}, \dfrac {-b} {a^2 + b^2} }$.
All the [[Axiom:Group Axioms|group axioms]] are thus seen to be fulfilled, and so $\tuple {E, \times_E}$ is a [[Definition:Group|group]].
It is sufficient to observe that:
{{eqn | q = \forall a, b, c, d \in F
| r = \tuple {a c - b d, a d + b c}
{{eqn | r = \tuple {c a - d b, c b + d a}
and it is seen that $\times_E$ is a [[Definition:Commutative Operation|commutative operation]].
It remains to be shown that $\times_E$ is [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributive]] over $+_E$.
{{eqn | q = \forall a, b, c, d, e, f \in F
{{eqn | r = \tuple {a \paren {c + e} - b \paren {d + f}, a \paren {d + f} + b \paren {c + e} }
{{eqn | r = \tuple {a c + a e - b d - b f, a d + a f + b c + b e}
| c = $F$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]]: $\times_F$ [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributes]] over $+_F$
{{eqn | r = \tuple {\paren {a c - b d} + \paren {a e - b f}, \paren {a d + b c} + \paren {a f + b e} }
{{eqn | r = \tuple {a c - b d, a d + b c} + \tuple {a e - b f, a f + b e}
Thus it has been demonstrated that $\times_E$ is [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributive]] over $+_E$.
All the criteria have been checked, and it follows that $\tuple {E, +_E, \times_E}$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].
